links.outcome: Differential diagnosis accuracy with physician reference evidence versus independent retrieval
links.effect: Up to 73.4% accuracy on differential diagnosis with physician reference evidence; as low as 25.4% when models relied on independent retrieval.
links.quote: Evaluations reveal a stark dichotomy: while advanced models demonstrate clinical reasoning proficiency when supplied with physician reference evidence (achieving up to $73.4\%$ accuracy on differential diagnosis), their performance substantially declines (as low as $25.4\%$) when reliant on independent retrieval mechanisms.

screen.reason: Evaluates MLLMs on a clinical benchmark comparing performance with physician-provided reference evidence (retrieval grounding) versus independent retrieval or standard reasoning.
